module_title: Input/Output Devices - Pointing Devices, Recognition Technologies, and Printers
introduction: This intermediate tier targets specialized input technologies heavily tested in banking and SSC exams (such as OMR and MICR) and breaks down the mechanical classification of printers (Impact vs. Non-Impact).

core_concepts.title: Specialized Recognition Devices
core_concepts.description:
- OMR (Optical Mark Recognition): Used to evaluate multiple-choice question (MCQ) answer sheets.
- OCR (Optical Character Recognition): Scans printed or handwritten text and converts it into machine-encoded, editable text.
- MICR (Magnetic Ink Character Recognition): Exclusively used by banks to quickly process and clear cheques.
- BCR (Barcode Reader): Used in retail to read the vertical black-and-white lines on products.

core_concepts.title: Pointing Devices
core_concepts.description: Besides the mouse, other devices used to control the cursor include: Trackball (often used in graphic design), Touchpad (built into laptops), Light Pen (allows drawing directly on a CRT screen), and Joystick (primarily used for flight simulators and gaming).

core_concepts.title: Impact Printers
core_concepts.description:
These function like traditional typewriters. A print head or pin physically strikes an ink ribbon against the paper to leave a mark. They are noisy and cannot print high-resolution graphics. 
Examples: Dot Matrix Printer and Daisy Wheel Printer.

core_concepts.title: Non-Impact Printers
core_concepts.description:
These form characters and images on a piece of paper without actually striking the page. They are fast, quiet, and produce high-quality graphics. 
Examples: Inkjet Printer (sprays liquid ink) and Laser Printer (uses a laser beam and dry powder toner).

important_entities.name: Plotter
important_entities.significance: A specialized output device used primarily by engineers, architects, and city planners to print large-scale, high-quality vector graphics, maps, and architectural blueprints.

important_entities.name: Standard QWERTY Layout
important_entities.significance: A standard Windows keyboard typically contains 104 keys, which includes 12 dedicated Function keys (F1 through F12) located at the top row.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Because 'Plotter' is an uncommon word, students often guess it is an input device or a storage drive. Remember: A Plotter is just a massive, high-precision printer. Therefore, it is strictly an OUTPUT device.
If asked to categorize a Dot Matrix printer, remember it is an 'Impact' printer and specifically a 'Character Printer' (it prints one character at a time, not a whole line or page).

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: The 'C' in MICR stands for 'Character' (Magnetic Ink Character Recognition), not 'Code'. This is a highly repeated trap in banking exams.

exam_strategy_tips: Master the exact full forms of OMR, OCR, and MICR. Examiners often swap words like 'Recognition' with 'Reader' to create confusing options. In MICR, it is always 'Recognition'.
